summary: ObjectGenome validates aggregate component mass against genome.massKg but treats genome.centerOfMassM only as an arbitrary finite point inside the object envelope. Because ComponentSpec exposes massKg and localPositionM but no separate component-COM offset, the authored reference-pose center of mass is derivable from the canonical component graph; allowing an unrelated declared centerOfMassM creates internally contradictory physical metadata. The permanent office-chair, utility-table, and filing-cabinet fixtures all currently demonstrate this drift, so correction must be versioned rather than silently rewriting fixture truth.
evidence: Generation-3 ObjectGenome primary branch agent/objects/HG-BACKFILL-OBJECTGENOME-v7k3m9-g3 validates componentMassKg against genome.massKg with tolerance, while centerOfMassM is checked only for finite Vec3 shape and containment inside dimensionsM.

ObjectGenome ComponentSpec already gives each canonical component massKg and localPositionM, and exposes no per-component center-of-mass offset; at the authored reference pose those fields define the available mass-distribution model.

The office-table fixture declares centerOfMassM.y=0.08 even though its four 2.4kg legs at y=-0.03, 2.0kg crossbar at y=0.15, and 15.4kg top at y=0.33 over total mass 27kg imply a substantially higher component-weighted reference-pose y center.

The office-chair and filing-cabinet fixtures likewise declare centerOfMassM values that are not the component-mass-weighted average of their own localPositionM values, proving this is existing canonical fixture drift rather than only a synthetic malformed input.

A repair should not be folded invisibly into the current generation-3 primary familyVersion/state-aliasing work: center-of-mass correction changes canonical recipe fingerprint/physical truth and therefore needs explicit fixture/version migration semantics plus deterministic regressions.
